headlines.title: French Yields Hit 5%, Highest Since 2002, as Risk Gauge Climbs
headlines.summary: French 10-year yields breaching 5% for the first time since 2002 is not a footnote — it is a SOVEREIGN STRESS signal that the consensus has been desperately papering over. Rising energy costs plus fiscal paralysis plus violent street protests is a cocktail that spreads to peripheral European debt, hammers EUR, and puts the ECB in an impossible position. Watch for contagion into Italian BTPs, European bank stocks, and any dollar-denominated safe-haven flows that accelerate the very dollar strength everyone claims is 'priced in.'

headlines.title: SpaceX up over 8% in premarket after earnings beat and Musk hints at Tesla tie-up
headlines.summary: SpaceX's blowout quarter is doing the EXACT job the AI bull market needed — a real revenue number to wave at the skeptics — and Musk dangling a Tesla-SpaceX megamerger is the kind of narrative grenade that sends both stocks into orbit before anyone has done the math. TSLA gets a free valuation re-rating on merger speculation alone, the broader neocloud complex gets a lifeline after last week's carnage, and NVDA catches a sympathy bid. The conspiracy-minded will note that a merger conveniently solves Musk's Tesla governance discount problem while locking retail into a story too big to short.

headlines.title: Oil prices climb as traders assess Middle East developments
headlines.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards mining the Strait of Hormuz is not a drill — roughly 20% of global oil supply transits that chokepoint, and even a CREDIBLE THREAT reprices energy risk across every sector that breathes diesel. United Airlines already slashed its 2026 profit outlook on fuel costs, UK CPI just printed 3.5% driven by motor fuels, and Indian Oil is scrambling to reroute Middle East imports. The feedback loop from higher energy into sticky inflation into rate-hike expectations is the one macro thread that ties together the French bond blowup, the Fed's next move, and every earnings guide that assumed $80 oil.
